chapter_note: A short, highly structured five-fold list of fire’s operations. Paragraph 1 contains a minimal dialogue/frame attribution (“Once more he speaks”), but the five-work teaching itself reads as impersonal, systematic exposition consistent with the older classificatory layer; no NT citation or institutional application appears.

paragraphs.core_text: This fire, which burns and is apparent today in the world, it does five works.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: “Once more he speaks:” (formulaic opening marker of the Kephalaia compilation frame).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The colon-introduced speech tag is a compilation-frame device; the remaining sentence introduces a numbered five-fold structure in an impersonal, expository voice.

paragraphs.core_text: The first work that it does is this: It incinerates and burns wood, and everything that shall be placed upon it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered, procedural description of how fire works; no citation, exhortation, or institutional vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: The second: It separates four aspects of the wood, which are these: fire and light, ash and smoke.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic analytical classification (second work; fourfold separation) characteristic of the integrated cosmological/scientific teaching style.

paragraphs.core_text: The third: It gives a taste and an {aroma} to whatever will be cooked on it. It also gives heat and cheer to whoever will be close to it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the enumerated list in the same impersonal explanatory register.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth work that [it] does: All craftsmen shall work the utensils that they will fabricate in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still within the numbered five-work scheme; practical exemplification but not church/pastoral regulation.

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth: It shall display light, and the people see by [it].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Closes the five-fold list; expository and non-citation-based.
